Quantitative measurements are obtained from high-speed visualizations of pool boiling at atmospheric
pressure from smooth and roughened surfaces, using a perfluorinated hydrocarbon (FC-77) as the working fluid.

Important bubble nucleation parameters during the pool boiling of FC-77 on smooth and rough surfaces are experimentally
investigated.

The insertion gap (inset,
Fig. 1a) surrounding the 25.4-mm square test piece was filled with
a high-temperature RTV silicone caulk.

Each test piece
consisted of an aluminum block into which twelve 3.18-mm diameter cartridge heaters were inserted in a distribution (Fig. 1b) that
ensured a uniform heat flux at the top of the test surface.

Input power to the test pieces was fixed for the four cases at 20 W,
40 W, 60 W, and 80 W, respectively. The measurements therefore
correspond to heat-flux controlled pool boiling.
using a perfluorinated hydrocarbon (FC-77) as the working fluid
